gaps.why_now: The dedicated Phase 9 build step is the smallest honest review gate for runtime pilot-module work.

The survey gate keeps the roadmap anchor, landed loader scaffold, the shared runtime-loader facade plus allocator/init-flow contract replay, shared request-surface proof, and remaining runtime-loader blocker explicit while the lane stays narrow.
A sample-backed lifecycle starter is the first honest runtime-facing step that can reuse existing atomic helpers without pretending the full module substrate already exists.
The Phase 9 roadmap explicitly calls for selftest hooks, and the bounded runtime_atomic64 sample already keeps that requirement reviewable through descriptor metadata plus runSelftest().
A dedicated Phase 9 test file keeps the starter sample reviewable and bounded around lifecycle transitions plus the selftest-facing atomic64 surface.
A narrow differential gate now captures selected atomic64_test.c expectations for wide-value exchange and cmpxchg behavior plus selftest-family coverage before any broader runtime substrate work.

A bounded sample-side loader scaffold now makes the existing requires_runtime_substrate contract reviewable through explicit entry and exit symbol names, a prepared four-field atomic64 payload summary snapshot replay, the shared `toSharedLoadPlan()` plus `runtime_loader.prepareRequest()` proof, and a no-substrate release path without pretending a real runtime loader already exists.
The roadmap's loadable runtime pilot module step still depends on a shared runtime substrate that can turn the bounded init, selftest, and exit handoff plan into a real loadable module path.
